meetings.title: 20th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: The agenda of today's meeting was to interview the candidates who satisfy the criteria mentioned in the Section 9 of Tax Administration Act (Law No. 3/2010) from the nominees submitted by the President for appointment of an individual to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, pursuant to Section 8(a) of Tax Administration Act (Law No. 3/2010), which is determined by the committee's administrative panel under Section 223(a) of the Standing Orders of the People’s Majlis. In this regard, the administrative panel presented the names of the eligible candidates, as well as the reasons why certain candidates failed to meet the eligibility requirements. Furthermore, following a request by the administrative panel for a committee decision regarding whether to permit the submission of additional documents beyond those submitted with the President’s letter, North Feydhoo Constituency member Ismail Nizar proposed to proceed with interviewing only those candidates found eligible by the panel, on the grounds that granting such an opportunity would prolong the process and establish an undesirable precedent and it was seconded by Faresmaathodaa Constituency member Ashraf Rasheed. Upon opening the proposal for voting, it was unanimously passed by all committee members present at the time of voting. Following the interviews conducted by the committee with the eligible candidates, members assigned marks as deemed appropriate. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdhooh proposed that candidates scoring an average of 75% (seventy-five percent) or above be deemed qualified for appointment to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, that the committee recommend appointing one of these candidates to the post, and that the committee report be submitted to the Majlis and it was seconded by Faresmaathodaa Constituency member Ashraf Rasheed. Upon opening the proposal for voting, it was unanimously passed by all committee members present at the time of voting. Details of votes taken in this meeting are in the "Votes" section of this page.

In addition, after being re-handed over to the airport, necessary equipments have been upgraded and it has been in operation till date, and every year an audit or inspection is conducted to determine whether the airport is operating in accordance with the certification standards of the Maldives Civil Aviation Authority. While efforts were underway to develop the airport to meet the standards of an international airport, both parties in discussion for the development of Kaadehdhoo Airport, have backed down due to the government’ announcement to develop an international airport in Gdh. Thinadhoo. The Chairman also stated that if the government wants to take over Kaadehdhoo Airport, they are ready to handover the airport and are ready to discuss the matter with the government. He added that setting up an international airport in the nearby vicinity would not be feasible and the airport would be profitable with a consolidated development to the region. Villa Air Pvt Ltd also noted that Kaadehdhoo Airport is a very old airport and the work on wear and tear is being stalled and action has been taken in the case of employees based on the company's HR policies.

Councilor insisted that to revise the rent of the land to according to valuation done by the Maldives Land and Surrey Authority's Land Valuation Committee which is of 60 laari per hector as the Horizon Fisheries Private Limited has unfair advantage as of now with a lower rent rate compared to other small business. The council has voted to propose minimum of 20 to 60 laari per hector per month as a rent value. He also stated that they want to see the facility in operation and the company does not have the capacity to do so. He also stated that the Ministry of Finance had issued a circular regarding transfer of agreements to the respective council’s name with the amendment to the Decentralization Act but the Ministry of Fisheries and Ocean Resources haven’t transferred the agreement to the council’s name.

In this regard, the minister stated that as per the agreement, the land rent must be revised every five years and the rent had to be revised in 2023, but it was not revised as they haven’t reached an agreement about the concerns of the Council. According to the existing agreement, rent of the land is 15 Laari per square foot, however, the council proposed to change it to a range of 20 to 60 Laari per month. The minister shared that Horizon Fisheries Limited had not yet offered a rent rate and it would not be feasible for a facility that had not been in operation to go along with rent rates proposed by the Council. Till the rent is revised again, the rent amount for 2023 and 2024 is deposited to the Council’s account at the rate of 15 Laari per sq ft. The Minister noted that Horizon Fisheries Limited had made huge investments in the establishment of a cold storage facility in Hoan’dedhdhoo and discussions were already underway on the issue of delay in bringing it into operation and only benefit from the facility right now is the rent income. Although the Hoan’dedhdhoo Cold Storage Facility has not been in operation, other projects are already initiated for the development of the fishing industry in the south region. In this regard, the minister highlighted that the project in Gd. Thinadhoo will be completed by next year and project in Gdh. Fiyori would be completed by the end of 2026.

meetings.title: 16th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee met with Drives Association of Maldives regarding letter sent by the Drivers Association of Maldives regarding their concerns over introduction of a taxi fleet by the government. In this regard, the association stated that the government's introduction of a taxi fleet would directly and indirectly impact independent taxi service providers. Furthermore, the taxi community's revenues will be affected, and companies that have invested in the sector will be constrained by the government’s decision. They stated that the government’s support is needed to develop the taxi service sector, and they alone cannot work to improve the quality of service provided and requires the support of the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation as well as the Maldives Police Service. Currently, there is no study conduct to find out what are the challenges in providing taxi services, especially within Male' city. They raised their concerns about difficulty for taxis to travel on male' roads, as taxis are not allowed to enter some roads due to vehicles parking issues, and requested to address these issues, to penalize offensive taxi drivers, to amend taxi regulations. Drivers’ association official revealed that they do not intend to create a hurdle for the government's efforts to provide better services to the people. However, requested to understand the losses that could be faced by taxi service providers and individuals and have discussions with them to resolve the issue.

meetings.summary: During today's meeting, the committee met with the Maldives Ports Limited and Ministry of Economic Development and Trade officials regarding issue raised by The Maldives Trade Association (MTA)’s concerns regarding Maldives Ports Limited's decision to shift back to charging certain fees in US dollars from 01st April. In this regard, MPL explained how the process works and reasons for their decision. During the meeting MPL stated that the stevedoring charge are charges levied on loading/unloading of cargo from ship to barge/jetty or vice versa by manual labour/equipment, and mostly goods are imported into the Maldives by CIF (cost, insurance, freight) or FOB (free on board) basis. And in CIF freighting, the consignee makes the payment to the shipping agent or operator in dollars and stevedoring charge is included in freight charges, when stevedoring charge was to be paid to MPL in Dhivehi rufiyaa, the shipping agent exchange aforementioned dollars at an increased price from dollar black market and pays it to MPL in Dhivehi rufiyaa. Furthermore, MPL informed that since 2011, MPL has been charging the stevedoring charge in Dhivehi rufiyaa and the two parties currently working as shipping agents in the Maldives, TTS and MSS, have been consulted before making this change. MPL stated that shipping agents had been informed about the company's decision in February 2024 after the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade gave permission to it and had given approximately one-and-a-half months' time from April 2024 before formally informing their decision to revert the Stevedoring charges to be paid in US dollars. Ministry of Economic Development and Trade revealed that no objection to charge stevedoring charge in US dollars was given because it was a business decision taken by MPL to resolve the company's difficulties in getting dollars and procuring the port machinery. Moreover, ministry made the decision as they do not foresee that businesses will have to spend extra money due to this change as the stevedoring charge will be paid with freight charges in advance and since those who bring goods through FOB were few and it was a small volume, it was not expected to have a major impact on the economy. To conclude MPL highlighted that the decision was necessary for the country's economy, because it seems to be detrimental to the economy of the Maldives to transfer the proceeds of MPL to another country after acquiring a profit from currency exchange in any form. In addition, this will make it easier for the company to operate, which is expected to increase the efficiency of the company and will in return benefit the country. Moreover, Noting that this change will ensure that the dollar will be circulated through Banks in Maldives at 15.42 Dhivehi rufiyaa exchange rate, which will help to resolve the black market issue of the dollar to an extent.

meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: During today's meeting, the committee met with the members of The Maldives Trade Association (MTA) upon their request to share their concerns with the committee regarding Maldives Ports Limited's decision to shift back to charging certain fees in US dollars from 01st April. In this regard, MTA raised their concerns about MPL’s sudden change to revert back to payment of fees in US Dollar from Maldivian Ruffiyya without any discussions with the businesses and stakeholders and an adequate timeframe before implementation. Furthermore, due to this change with the shortage in dollar market, businesses are forced to buy US dollars at a higher rate than the market rate which in return will affect the prices of the goods and services and small business adversely. Moreover, MTA stated that this is not the right time for this change as the economy is struggling and especially when there is severe shortage in US dollar in the economy.
